mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 15% in the same month signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < previous month - 15%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately compressing profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production (INDPRO) decline of more than 1% from the previous month, sustained for two consecutive months, signals a contraction in economic output, which reduces corporate sales and earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month - 1% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.4%) in at least 65% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in CPIAUCSL of more than 0.5% signals a deflationary shock, which increases real interest rates and discourages investment, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.2%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase of more than 2% in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and a monthly decline of more than 3% in retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) signals a divergence between income growth and consumption, which often precedes a consumer confidence drop and negative equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month + 2% AND RSAFS < previous month - 3%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payroll employment (PAYEMS) increase of less than 50,000 while the unemployment rate (UNRATE) simultaneously rises signals a softening labor market, which reduces wage growth and inflation pressure, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as discount rate expectations decline.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent quarterly increase in real GDP (GDPC1) of more than 2% for three consecutive quarters signals a robust demand environment, which supports corporate earnings growth and justifies higher equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 quarterly change > 2% for 3 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 65% of triggered episodes.
